claim_under_audit.title: The Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer Conjecture for Analytic Rank Two: A Complete Proof via Definite Anticyclotomic Iwasawa Theory
claim_under_audit.author: Wang Xiong
claim_under_audit.bounded_search_note: No arXiv copy or later independently reviewed version was located in the bounded current search; this is not a completeness claim.
selectors_checked: Definition 6.1: (K1)-(K4), especially every ell|N splits in K and claimed epsilon(E/K)=+1 definite
Proposition 6.3: claimed implication from the Heegner/all-split condition to epsilon(E/K)=+1
Section 6.4 table: claimed N^- parity versus definite/indefinite quaternion algebra and root sign
level-raising discussion where one inert auxiliary prime is used to move between claimed vertices

primary_cross_checks.claim_checked: For an elliptic curve over Q and imaginary quadratic K with quadratic character epsilon, the sign of L(E/K,s) is -epsilon(N); epsilon(N)=-1 is the definite case and epsilon(N)=+1 is the indefinite case.
The relevant anticyclotomic theorem cell is explicitly indefinite and its Selmer dual has Lambda-rank one, with lambda-comparison hypotheses stated separately.

Under the Heegner hypothesis that every conductor prime splits in K, the anticyclotomic Selmer object is rank one over the Iwasawa algebra rather than the torsion/definite object asserted by the audited claim.

derivation: If every ell|N splits in K, then epsilon(ell)=+1 for every conductor prime and hence epsilon(N)=+1.
Howard's sign formula gives epsilon(E/K)=-epsilon(N)=-1, i.e. the indefinite vertex.
Therefore the audited preprint's all-split hypothesis cannot simultaneously imply sign +1/definite as asserted in Proposition 6.3 and the Section 6.4 table.

Equivalently, N^-=1 has zero inert conductor primes; the associated quaternion algebra is indefinite at infinity, while adding one inert level-raising prime toggles to the definite vertex rather than the reverse.
source_bound_result.scope: This refutes the audited proof route/certificate as written. It does not refute BSD, prove nonexistence of another rank-two proof, or establish a literature-wide negative result.
